key_catalyst: Alphabet -4% after-hours on raised $195-205B capex guidance despite a Q2 beat, joined by Tesla's 18% profit decline and negative free cash flow
reasoning: Three independent bearish catalysts converged overnight: Alphabet fell 4%+ after-hours on a capex guidance raise to $195-205B (a top-6 QQQ holding), Tesla missed badly with an 18% profit decline, negative free cash flow and a 35% EPS miss, and Brent topped $95 after Iran rejected talks while the 30-year yield held above 5% with September hike odds at 83%. Unlike 2026-07-22, when oil above $95 and a 4.64% 10-year were offset by bullish AI news (Super Micro's $60B in orders, AMD-Anthropic), today's AI-thesis news flipped negative, removing the offset that limited that day's loss to -0.51%. The -1.58% pre-market gap shows the market is already responding, but the catalysts are unresolved and Intel/IBM still report into a rate-hike-pricing tape.
